answer: An ember certificate binds a manufacturer-certified, nonexportable chip serial to one paid key. At an unpredictable shared pulse, validators send nonces through each device inlet and check signed live quotes; duplicate serials void both slots. A farm can rent chips, but k keys require k certified devices at once plus k distinct 30-epoch deposits, each above capped seat pay; leases and loans cannot reuse either resource. If a quote is missing, pay is zero; forgery burns its deposit. Issuers certify serials and validators enforce this proposal, not MinePoA today.
